questions.prompt: You've deployed an e- commerce website using Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The website domain name is myshoppingweb.com.Your client requires that customers can access the site using both: myshoppingweb.com (the root domain), and www.myshoppingweb.com (the subdomain) You are managing DNS using Amazon Route 53. Which configuration should you set up in Route 53 to fulfill this requirement?
options: Create a CNAME record for myshoppingweb.com pointing to the ALB, and an Alias record for wmn.'.myshoppingweb.com pointing to the ALB
Create a CNAME record for myshoppingweb.com and a CNAME record for 'mwv.myshoppingwebcom
Create an Alias record for myshoppingweb.com and a CNAME record for www.myshoppingweb.com
Create an A record for myshoppingweb.com and an AAAA record for www.myshoppingweb.com
explanations: The apex record is a CNAME, which DNS does not permit. An alias for www does not repair the invalid apex.
Both records are CNAMEs, so the root-domain record remains invalid even though a CNAME for www is allowed.
The alias supports the root domain and tracks the ALB endpoint. The www CNAME can point to that endpoint or the root name.
Ordinary A/AAAA records require IP addresses; an ALB has changing addresses and should be targeted with aliases or a valid subdomain CNAME.
questions.takeaway: A CNAME cannot live at the zone apex. A Route 53 alias can point the apex to an ALB; a CNAME is valid for www.

options: Move the instances to a public subnet with a route to the Internet Gateway
ploy an AWS NAT Gateway in a public subnet and update the private subnet's route table to use it for internet-bound traffic
Launch an additional EC2 instance in a public subnet and use it as a bastion host for downloads
Create a VPN connection to a data center and route outbound traffic through the on-premises firewall
explanations: Moving instances and adding direct internet routing changes the private placement; it is not the requested private-subnet egress solution.
Place the public NAT gateway in a public subnet with an internet route, then route private-subnet outbound traffic to it. Instances need no public IPv4 addresses.
A bastion is for controlled administration, not automatically a NAT/proxy for all downloads, and introduces host management.
Routing through on-premises infrastructure can be built, but adds dependency and routing complexity compared with the native NAT gateway option.
questions.takeaway: A public NAT gateway gives private instances outbound IPv4 internet access without accepting unsolicited inbound internet connections to those instances.
questions.note: Choose an availability-aware NAT design. NAT does not replace security groups, endpoint controls or restrictions on egress destinations.

questions.prompt: A photo-processing pipeline uses an S3 bucket to store uploaded images and an Amazon SQS queue to notify an ECS cluster of new jobs. Each task processes exactly one image, and processing time is consistent. During peak periods, the queue backlog grows significantly. Which CloudWatch metric should drive the auto scaling of ECS tasks to handle the workload efficiently?
options: The number of objects in the S3 bucket
Memory utilization of the ECS container tasks
The number of visible messages in the SQS queue
The number of running ECS tasks
explanations: The total S3 object count includes already processed images and does not directly measure waiting jobs.
Memory usage may remain stable even while queued work grows; it is not the direct workload-backlog signal.
Visible SQS messages measure work waiting to be processed and can drive scaling. With consistent processing time, normalize by task count for backlog-per-task target tracking.
The running-task count measures capacity, not the amount of pending work that should trigger more capacity.
questions.takeaway: Queue backlog reflects pending work. For target tracking, backlog per running worker/task is generally more useful than an unnormalized total.
questions.note: Use ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible with an appropriate per-task backlog target and maximum acceptable queue latency. Consider startup time and scale-in protection.

explanations: A NAT gateway provides a path to public endpoints and does not satisfy the private hybrid transfer requirement.
A DataSync agent using the private VPC endpoint over Direct Connect supplies managed transfer through a private network path to supported storage locations.
Offline devices require shipping/handling and do not supply the requested scalable online migration path; device eligibility/availability also needs review.
Lambda does not directly mount arbitrary on-premises NFS shares as a general replacement for DataSync; the proposal omits supported connectivity and transfer management.
questions.takeaway: DataSync private endpoints plus private hybrid connectivity can transfer supported on-premises data without routing the data path over the public internet.
questions.note: Direct Connect is private connectivity, not automatic encryption. DataSync uses encryption in transit; validate every required endpoint and data/control path.

Place the database EC2 instance in a private subnet with no route to an internet gateway or public IP
Create a separate security group for the database instance that allows inbound Oracle traffic only from the web server's security group
Assign a public IP to the database instance and configure its security group to allow inbound Oracle traffic from 0.0.0.0/0
explanations: Putting the database in the public tier fails the requested network segmentation even if a security-group rule limits some access.
A private subnet and no public address prevent direct internet reachability of the database instance.
Referencing the web-tier security group on the database port permits only the intended application tier without relying on broad public CIDRs.
A public IP and a database-port rule open to 0.0.0.0/0 directly violate the database isolation requirement.

Schedule an AWS Step Functions state machine to poll the table for new items and call the downstream microservice
explanations: Write-capacity metrics are aggregated signals and do not identify each changed item's contents or reliably trigger one action per transaction.

Amazon RDS creates a full snapshot every 12 hours and stores transaction logs in Amazon S3 once per hour

You must manually enable transaction log backups in RDS to use point-in-time restore features

The stated twelve-hour snapshot and hourly-log schedule does not describe the normal RDS automated-backup mechanism.
Point-in-time restore reconstructs state from the snapshot and subsequent transaction logs up to an available restore time.
Logs are backed up outside the snapshot window as well; discarding them afterward would prevent continuous point-in-time recovery.

questions.prompt: A multinational corporation needs to collect and analyze badge-swipe data from more than 10k sensors located in offices around the world. Each sensor sends a 20 KB JSON payload every 5 seconds. The solution must ingest and process this streaming data in near real time, perform analytics (for example, calculate the total time that employees spend in the office) and store the results for dashboards. The architecture must be highly scalable and durable as new sensors are added. Which combination of AWS services provides the most appropriate solution? (Select TWO)
options: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with enough shards to handle the incoming throughput. Develop a consumer application (such as AWS Lambda or an EC2 fleet) to process the stream data in parallel and publish the aggregated results
Use Amazon Data Firehose to deliver the raw or processed data into Amazon Redshift or Amazon S3 for analytics and visualization
Use an Amazon SQS queue to decouple ingestion and a fleet of EC2 instances to poll and process the messages
Use Amazon SimpleDB to ingest the streaming JSON payload and run aggregate queries
explanations: A correctly sized stream and parallel consumers support the incoming telemetry rate and near-real-time processing. Provision capacity based on bytes and record counts.
Firehose provides managed delivery to supported destinations such as S3 and Redshift, fitting the storage/analytics part of the pipeline.
SQS plus EC2 can form a work-processing design but is not the preferred pair for the retained, scalable streaming analytics and delivery pattern described.
SimpleDB is not a purpose-built high-throughput streaming ingestion and aggregation service.
questions.takeaway: Use Kinesis Data Streams for parallel ingestion/consumption and Firehose for managed delivery of records into storage/analytics destinations.
questions.note: At 10,000 sensors × 20 KB every 5 seconds the raw rate is about 40 MB/s before overhead. Size shard/consumer capacity and account for partition-key distribution.

questions.prompt: During a security audit, a company discovered that several objects uploaded to an Amazon S3 bucket did not have encryption enabled. The security team requires that all objects be encrypted with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys and wants to understand how S3 encryption works. Which statement about server-side encryption with AWS KMS (SSE-KMS) is correct?
options: AWS KMS encrypts data only when it is transmitted to the client; data at rest in Amazon S3 remains unencrypted
SSE-KMS encrypts objects at rest in Amazon S3. S3 encrypts the object before saving it on disk and decrypts it when the data is accessed
SSE-KMS restricts the use of KMS keys to AWS services only; users and applications cannot request decryption
AWS KMS automatically grants decrypt permissions on all KMS keys to every AWS account in the organization by default
explanations: SSE-KMS is encryption at rest, not a replacement for TLS in transit. Objects stored with it are encrypted on storage.
S3 handles object encryption before persistent storage and decryption during authorized retrieval, with KMS protecting the data-encryption keys.
Authorized applications and users can use KMS operations and retrieve SSE-KMS objects; permissions are not reserved exclusively for AWS services.
KMS does not grant every account in an organization blanket decrypt rights. Key policies, identity policies and other controls must authorize access.
questions.takeaway: SSE-KMS uses envelope encryption for S3 data at rest. Read/write permissions and KMS key authorization remain separate controls.
questions.note: New S3 uploads are encrypted by default with SSE-S3; requiring KMS keys is a stronger, specific requirement. Changing defaults does not retroactively convert all existing objects.
questions.title: SSE-KMS uses envelope encryption for S3 data at rest
